svg.title: What happens inside POST /v1/quests/generate
svg.desc: A request carrying coarse coordinates, minutes available, radius, mood, sanitized interests and a persona enters the API. The Context Builder adds local time, daylight left and weather, deciding indoor_only. The Scout searches a three by three block of geohash-5 cells with Atlas vector search, post-filters by haversine distance and safety and time rules, and caps candidates at three per place kind for a maximum of eight. A memory check drops themes done in the last fourteen days. The Quest Master, a fine-tuned open-weight model on llama.cpp, is called with JSON-schema constrained decoding. Its draft runs through validators V1 to V12; one failure triggers a single retry with the failure reasons appended, and a second failure, a timeout or an unreachable model hands over to a deterministic fallback engine. Only then does the server assign the id, rarity and XP, hydrate the place, store the quest and return it with an X-Quest-Source header saying llm or fallback.
svg.text: One quest, step by step: POST /v1/quests/generate
Server-authoritative. The model writes prose and picks a place from a list. It never decides an id, a rarity or a point of XP.
Request in
lat/lng at 3 decimals, minutes 10 to 180, radius 300 to 6000 m,
mood and persona from enums, interests sanitized to plain keywords
Context Builder (deterministic)
part of day, weekday, daylight minutes left, Open-Meteo weather
sets indoor_only on storm, rain, 38 C heat or under 35 min of daylight
Scout: find real places
centre cell + 8 neighbours (geohash-5), Atlas $vectorSearch on 384-dim
BGE-small vectors, haversine cut, safety and walk-time filters, 3 per kind
Memory check: do not repeat yourself
$vectorSearch on memories filtered to this device and the last 14 days,
drops places and themes already done. Result: 8 candidates at most.
Quest Master: the open-weight model
byte-identical system prompt + context JSON + candidates, temp 0.8,
top_p 0.95, max_tokens 380, timeout 25 s, json_schema constrained
Validators: the only gate that matters
Pure functions. The same code filters training data and scores the eval,
so a rule can never be true in one place and false in another.
passes
Server assigns the game state
rarity from minutes and distance, XP from the published formula, uuid,
place hydrated from the candidate it picked. Caps and streaks applied.
Store and answer
written to quests with source llm or fallback and a request digest that
holds no location. The X-Quest-Source header says which engine wrote it.
The twelve rules every quest must pass
V1 parses as JSON and matches the Pydantic schema
V2 place_id was copied from the candidate list, or is null
V3 est_minutes is at least 5 and fits the time you have
V4 banned-term lint, written to catch paraphrases
V5 safety_note is present and 10 to 140 characters
V6 a photo prompt is never about a person
V7 lengths, 70-word briefing cap, no emoji, no hashtags
V8 no URL, email address or phone number anywhere
V9 indoor_only weather means an indoor place or none
V10 a daylight-only place needs daylight actually left
V11 category is one of the seven in the enum
V12 not a near-duplicate of a quest from the last 14 days
first failure: one retry, failure reasons appended
twice, timed out, or model unreachable
Fallback engine (no network, no model)
Deterministic templates per place kind and category, flavoured by
persona. Property-tested to always pass V1 to V11, and tested against
all 104 red-team contexts. Same seed in, same quest out.
The player is never shown an error. /v1/quests/generate is required
to succeed with the whole model service switched off.
